## EA Media Tools 2.2.0 - jaguar

### Adaptive batch correction

- The first 10-second average from the initial single encode now establishes a fixed concurrency ceiling.
- The ceiling is `floor(average FPS / 200)`, bounded by the available jobs and supported NVENC session limit.
- A baseline around 900 FPS therefore permits at most four simultaneous encodes; 710 FPS permits three.
- Later aggregate FPS samples may delay adding another encode when performance drops, but cannot increase the first measurement's ceiling.
- Completed slots continue taking queued episodes without recalculating the session ceiling.
- Cancel All stops active FFmpeg processes and interrupts both replacement cooldowns and the adaptive sampler, preventing another queued encode from launching.

### Validation

- Added regression coverage for a 900 FPS baseline followed by inflated aggregate reports, plus queue-wide adaptive cancellation.
- Lint, native and compatibility TypeScript checks, unit tests, and production packaging.

[Review the correction since v2.1.0](https://github.com/eaforlife/media-converter/compare/v2.1.0...v2.2.0).
